# Gash — full digest

Source: https://github.com/Xmar1881/Gash
License: AGPL-3.0-only
Status: experimental, `v0.1.0-dev`
This file is a single-fetch, self-contained summary of the project for LLM and
agent ingestion. It mirrors the repository documentation; where the two differ,
the repository files are authoritative.

## What Gash is

Gash is a Go-native, plugin-driven web security scanner. Its defining design
choice is that **plugins propose candidates and engine-owned oracles decide
findings**. Every plugin — a YAML file, a sandboxed JavaScript file, or a
trusted native binary — compiles to the same `PluginSpec` intermediate
representation and flows through one pipeline:

```
Candidate -> Oracle -> Evidence -> Finding
```

A candidate carries an injection point and a proposed payload. An engine oracle
then verifies it with a control comparison, repeat rules, and baseline gating.
If the oracle does not accept, there is no finding. A plugin cannot declare its
own severity into existence, cannot self-confirm, and cannot reach the engine's
internal state: it only uses capabilities exposed on the request environment.

## Who it is for, and who it is not for

- Good fit: CI security gates, internal assessments, and plugin development
  where a small, auditable core matters and evidence must be reproducible.
- Poor fit: unsupervised production scanning, or compliance reporting that
  requires a mature, widely-audited toolchain.

Gash is **not** a drop-in replacement for Nuclei, OWASP ZAP, or Burp Suite. It
competes on verification discipline, not on library size or maturity.

## Verified catalog facts

- 328 plugins in the reference catalog:
  - 275 Tier 1 YAML plugins,
  - 52 Tier 2 sandboxed JavaScript plugins,
  - 1 Tier 3 native gRPC PoC.
- Plus 13 engine-owned detectors that ship behind a detector port
  (`internal/detector`) rather than as plugin files, because their transport or
  input cannot be expressed in YAML or the JS sandbox: JavaScript recon, content
  discovery, SPA embedded-state secrets, development build markers, HTTP request
  smuggling, and protocol probes for TLS, DNS, TCP banner, SSH banner/handshake,
  and database ports/authentication.
- Every reference plugin ships positive and negative fixtures and a precision
  report under `docs/metrics/`.
- Counts are verifiable with `go run ./cmd/gash plugins list`.

## Engine-owned oracles

Confidence is decided by engine oracles, not by plugins. The vocabulary
includes: `reflection`, `stored`, `execution`, `error`, `differential`,
`timing`, `oob`, `header`, `cookie`, `cors`, `redirect`, `version`,
`upload-served`, `verb-tamper`, and `middleware-bypass`.

Each oracle enforces its own proof rules; a plugin only chooses which oracle to
ask. Examples of the discipline:

- A reflection claim needs a recognizable execution payload plus a clean
  control; a bare canary in the response is at most tentative.
- A differential claim needs three stable true reads, three stable false reads,
  a divergence, and a control that is not the true branch.
- A timing claim needs a median delay above the declared floor that also passes
  a statistical test; timing never exceeds `firm`.
- An OOB claim needs a matched one-time correlation token; without a
  self-hosted server the plugin returns nothing instead of guessing.
- A stored-XSS claim needs a write exchange that was accepted, a render that
  carries the payload in an executable context, and a clean sibling control.
- An upload claim needs an accepted upload, the artifact served back with the
  planted canary, and a clean control URL; the served content type then decides
  `confirmed` (active content) or `firm` (inert).

## Evidence ladder

```
tentative  ->  firm  /  static-execution-evidence  ->  confirmed
```

- `tentative`: a lead that is not yet proven (hidden by default in reports).
- `firm`: a strong single-channel signal.
- `static-execution-evidence`: a parser-verified executable payload plus a clean
  control, without running a browser.
- `confirmed`: the strongest level; for XSS it requires the `-tags deep` build
  with a headless browser, a real trigger, and a clean control.

Timing-based findings never exceed `firm`. The ladder has no plugin-defined rung.

## Plugin tiers

| Tier | Format | Model | Trust | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tier 1 | YAML (`.yaml`) | One request, declarative | Auto-discovered, no trust step | Single-step checks only |
| Tier 2 | JavaScript (`.js`) | goja VM sandbox | Auto-discovered, no trust step | Multi-step logic, correlations, raw JSON/multipart bodies; parameters declared in an `oracle_params` block |
| Tier 3 | Native (`.gashplugin.yaml` + binary) | gRPC over HashiCorp go-plugin | Never runs on discovery alone: SHA-256 pinned and explicitly trusted via `gash plugins trust` | No raw sockets; all network access flows through host-provided capabilities |

Plugins are drop-in: placing a `.yaml` or `.js` file under `~/.gash/plugins/`
(or `GASH_PLUGIN_PATH`) is enough. There is no `--load-plugin` or `--enable`
flag. Tier 3 binaries additionally require an explicit trust record.

## Install

```sh
# Latest release
go install github.com/Xmar1881/Gash/cmd/gash@latest

# From source
git clone https://github.com/Xmar1881/Gash.git
cd Gash
go build ./cmd/gash
```

The standard build needs no CGO. Only the deep (headless browser) build uses
`chromedp` and is built with `-tags deep`.

## Quickstart

```sh
# List the discovered catalog
./gash plugins list

# Validate and fixture-test one plugin
./gash plugins validate plugins/xss/xss-reflected-basic.js
./gash plugins test plugins/xss/xss-reflected-basic.js

# Scan a target you own or are authorized to test
./gash scan --target http://localhost:8080 --scope localhost

# Active profile, JSON report
./gash scan --target http://localhost:8080 --scope localhost --active --format json --output report.json

# Deep profile with headless verification (requires the deep build)
./gash scan --target http://localhost:8080 --scope localhost --profile deep --browser-verify

# Fail a CI job on firm-or-higher findings, emit SARIF
./gash scan --target ... --format sarif --output report.sarif --fail-on firm
```

Other entry points: `gash menu` (interactive console), `gash bench run`
(dataset scoring), `gash bench lab up` (local lab), `gash diff`, `gash suppress`,
`gash plugins new <id> --tier yaml|js` (scaffold).

## Safety defaults

- The CLI default profile is `standard` (controlled active checks); `--profile
  safe` is strictly passive (GET/HEAD/OPTIONS).
- `--profile deep`, `--profile aggressive`, `--active`-only checks, and OOB are
  explicit opt-ins.
- Out-of-band callbacks are self-hosted only and disabled by default; blind
  plugins skip honestly with `oob-not-configured`.
- Without `--scope`, the crawler and redirects stay on the target's registrable
  domain (eTLD+1); `--allow-external` restores open mode. `--scope` pins an
  explicit CIDR/domain allowlist, blocks out-of-scope redirects, and pins DNS
  (rebinding protection).
- The interactive menu (`gash menu`, TR/EN) exposes the same controls: tabbed
  scan/plugin/bench/OpenAPI/diff/suppress/console/status/help screens, bulk
  target files, proxy modes, auth modes, redacted command preview, and repeat
  last command.
- Scan only systems you own or have written permission to test.

## Quality gates enforced in CI

- Fixture precision gate: a plugin's fixtures must reach precision ≥ 0.99.
- Corpus gate: any `firm`-or-higher false positive on the clean corpus fails the
  build.
- Detector-inventory parity: the runtime detector registry and
  `docs/detector-inventory.md` must match, checked by a contract test.
- Static and supply-chain gates: `go vet`, `gofmt`, `gosec`, `govulncheck`,
  race tests, and a benchmark gate.

## How Gash differs (honest comparison)

Gash is experimental and small. The table below is a positioning statement, not
a performance claim.

| Capability | Gash | Nuclei | OWASP ZAP | Burp Suite |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Primary use | Engine + oracle-gated plugin runner (CI/CLI) | Fast template-based scanner with a huge library | Full proxy, spider, passive + active scanner | Manual-first intercepting proxy + scanner |
| Plugin model | Drop-in single file (YAML/JS auto, native explicit trust) | YAML templates, large community registry | Add-ons / scripts / automation framework | BApp extensions, manual workflows |
| Who decides a finding | Engine-owned oracles only; plugins emit candidates | Template matchers + severity declarations | Scan rules + alert confidence | Scanner checks + analyst review |
| False-positive discipline | Corpus gate (any `firm+` = build fail), precision ≥ 0.99 gate, control + repeat rules | Severity/filtering conventions, community QA | Alert risk/confidence taxonomy | Manual verification workflow |
| Blind / OOB | Self-hosted OOB only, explicit opt-in, honest skip | Interactsh integration (incl. public server option) | OOB via add-ons / callback channels | Burp Collaborator (built-in, SaaS-backed) |
| Maturity | Early, small reference set, lab recall measured manually | Mature, thousands of templates, wide adoption | Mature, OWASP flagship, broad protocol support | Industry standard for manual pentest (commercial) |
| License / cost | AGPL-3.0-only, free and open | Open (Nuclei + templates), free | Open (Apache 2.0), free | Commercial (Community free tier) |

Use Nuclei for template breadth, ZAP for proxy/crawl coverage, and Burp for
manual depth. Use Gash when you want a small, auditable core where no plugin can
mint a finding without engine-grade evidence.

## Frequently asked questions

**What is Gash?**
A Go-native, plugin-driven web security scanner whose core philosophy is that
plugins propose candidates while engine-owned oracles decide findings. No plugin
can mint a finding without engine-grade evidence (control comparison, repeat
rules, baseline gating).

**Is Gash production-ready?**
No — it is experimental (`v0.1.0-dev`). The core architecture is stable, but the
plugin set is still growing, real-world recall is measured only on lab targets,
the deep (browser) build requires Chrome/Chromium, and the API may change before
`v1.0.0`.

**How is Gash different from Nuclei, ZAP, or Burp?**
Finding authority sits with engine oracles rather than template matchers or
scanner rules; plugins are single drop-in files; false-positive discipline is a
build gate (precision ≥ 0.99 and zero `firm+` corpus false positives); OOB is
self-hosted only and skips honestly; and the license is AGPL-3.0-only.

**Why do I get no findings on a known-vulnerable target?**
Common causes: the target is out of `--scope`; the passive `safe` profile was
selected, so try `--profile standard`, `--profile deep`, or
`--profile aggressive`; the plugin is not loaded (check
`gash plugins list`); OOB is not configured for a blind plugin; or the rate limit
and request budget are too low.

**What does `--scope` do?**
Without `--scope` the scanner runs open: it follows redirects and crawl links to
any host and scheme. With `--scope example.com`, only `example.com` and its
subdomains are requested, out-of-scope redirects are blocked, DNS is pinned
against rebinding, and only HTTP→HTTPS upgrades are followed.

**Do I need CGO?**
No. `CGO_ENABLED=0` is recommended for static binaries. Only the deep build
(`-tags deep`, chromedp) needs CGO.
